question: Can the task-relevant slice inside the fixed eight upstream modules be identified by target-versus-control response geometry and transfer to held-out target rows?
discovery: Within each target task, even rows are discovery and odd rows are sealed target validation. Endpoint-matched C discovery/validation halves remain as frozen in the matched-control atlas.
fit: Per site, fit rank-8 generic-control PCA on C discovery response deltas. Remove that subspace from target-discovery response deltas, then fit target-residual PCA. Frozen retained target ranks are 1, 4, and 8. No validation row or causal outcome selects a basis.
intervention: On target-validation and C-validation rows, patch only the projection of donor-minus-base site responses onto the fitted target-residual basis. Compare with the full-response rank-0 eight-site program on the same rows.

predictions.pred_a_authority_split_alignment_finiten: Authorities, disjoint splits, exact endpoints, nondegenerate spectra, finiteness, and <=16 forwards close.
predictions.pred_b_full_response_validation_program_: Rank0 has worst held-out target residual <=0.05.
predictions.pred_c_target_basis_preserves_heldout_be: At rank 4 or 8, worst target residual <=0.15 and signed behavior projection >=0.80 in both tasks.
predictions.pred_d_target_basis_is_selective: The same rank moves C validation by <=10% of target full-effect scale in both tasks.
predictions.pred_e_basis_beats_control_complement: The same rank has no worse target residual and at least 50% lower worst C fraction than the control-complement rank 8.

decision: A pass promotes the response-split circuit to fresh-construction and weight-reader compilation. A null closes linear within-module response splitting for this program and redirects to conditional/nonlinear gates or a different causal boundary.
